title: Texas Locked a Foreign Company's Domain Over Missing Digital ID Checks
excerpt: Fourteen days after a Travis County judge signed, motherless.com dropped out of the .com zone file for every person on earth, most of whom have never heard of Travis County.
content_html:
Fourteen days after a Travis County judge signed, motherless.com dropped out of the .com zone file for every person on earth, most of whom have never heard of Travis County.

In Travis County, Texas, a judge has frozen motherless.com, the .com domain of a foreign pornography operator, taking it down worldwide until it posts a $9.14 million bond and builds an age verification digital ID system to the state's own specification.

Kick Online Entertainment is a foreign corporation, and the order admits so, which is the reason the writ went somewhere else. A state court cannot summon a company overseas, but it can order the American firm that keeps the registry of every .com name, and that registry is what makes a domain resolve at all.

We obtained a copy of the order for you here.

The case turns on HB 1181, Texas's age-verification law for adult sites. That firm is Verisign, a nonparty to it, and Judge Maya Guerra Gamble signed the writ of attachment on June 4, 2026, filed four days later in State of Texas v Kick Online Entertainment.

The order directs Verisign to place motherless.com on "a registry lock, hold, or similar status until replevied by Defendant," the legal term for the operator posting a bond to get its domain back.

The domain is frozen rather than taken, though the difference means little here. What Verisign actually applied on was serverHold plus server-level prohibitions on deleting, transferring and updating the name. A hold pulls motherless.com out of the .com zone file, so it resolves for nobody.

Kick must post a bond of $9,140,000, and that bond is "conditioned on Defendant's implementation of age verification that conforms with Texas Civil Practice and Remedies code chapter 129B," together with an affirmation that it will satisfy the civil penalties entered against it on September 30, 2024. A company outside the state's reach is being made to both pay and obey a Texas statute before its property comes back. This is specific performance of a state law, pulled from a foreign operator by holding an asset hostage at the registry.

Among the court's stated reasons the writ is "appropriate and justified" is the finding that "Defendant is not a resident of this state and is a foreign corporation," which turns the state's inability to reach a company into a ground for taking its property.

The order then pre-authorizes more of the same, closing with the line that "as many writs as the State deems necessary shall issue," so the count of future seizures is set by the attorney general and not by a judge weighing each one. And Texas was excused from the security these writs normally demand, because the order says "the State of Texas is not required to post a bond prior to the issuance of the Writ of Attachment."

The party taking the asset posts nothing. The party losing it posts $9.14 million.

A domain lock has no borders. The law reaches only Texas users, yet locking a .com pulls the site down for everyone on earth, including people in countries that never passed such a law, had no say in it and don't see why they have to have Texas law affect their lives. A state remedy has been given global effect only because the registry that happens to hold the record is American.

The site had been offline once already, over graver allegations. Dutch prosecutors took it down in May and opened a criminal case over alleged sexual abuse videos, after the broadcasters NOS and Nieuwsuur found it hosted on Dutch servers. The abuse reporting bureau Offlimits had logged 142 reports on the site this year, 25 of them involving children. Motherless returned about a week later, saying it had strengthened moderation. That takedown reached the site through its host and rested on a criminal case, where the Texas writ reaches it through the registry and rests on an unpaid civil penalty.

The precedent is what the attorney general wanted, and he says so. Paxton called the order a "huge precedent that websites can be stripped of their domain if they ignore the law and harm children with pornographic content."

His office said the writ "demonstrates that Texas has the legal authority and the proven tools to reach beyond its borders and hold foreign operators accountable" and that the state would use "every available legal mechanism, including writs of attachment against domain names," against any company "regardless of where it is incorporated." Nothing in the order confines the tool to pornography, so any Texas civil penalty against any foreign website is now collectable the same way.

We have previously argued that UK speech regulator Ofcom oversteps when it enforces the UK Online Safety Act against American services with no UK presence, and the same principle is at stake here.

Verisign is American and must obey an American court, so the legal hook is real in a way Ofcom's is not. The objection is not that the order is lawless, but that the .com registry on American soil hands American courts a switch for the whole internet, and a Travis County judge has now thrown it.

Unlike the UK Ofcom case, using American infrastructure, with its supposed First Amendment protections, are of no use here when a Texas judge can order a site taken down for hosting legal content, because it did not introduce digital ID features.

Kick never showed up in court. The company did not contest the suit, the civil penalties were entered by default on September 30, 2024, and no court has weighed Texas's arguments against an opposing party. The statute behind the bond condition, chapter 129B, is HB 1181, which the Supreme Court upheld last year in Free Speech Coalition v Paxton. Gamble's order is a trial court ruling that binds nobody outside this case.

sentences.en: Gamble's order is a trial court ruling that binds nobody outside this case.
sentences.zh: 甘布尔的命令是初审法院的一项裁决，对本案之外的任何人都没有约束力。

content_html_zh:
特拉维斯县法官签署协议十四天后，motherless.com 就退出了地球上所有人的 .com 区域档案，其中大多数人从未听说过特拉维斯县。

在德克萨斯州特拉维斯县，一名法官冻结了 motherless.com（一家外国色情内容运营商的 .com 域名），并在全球范围内将其关闭，直到该公司交纳 914 万美元的保证金并按照该州自己的规范建立年龄验证数字 ID 系统。

Kick Online Entertainment 是一家外国公司，该命令也承认这一点，这就是令状转移到其他地方的原因。 州法院不能传唤海外公司，但它可以命令美国公司保留每个 .com 名称的注册表，而该注册表才是域名解析的根本。

我们在这里为您获取了一份订单副本。

此案涉及德克萨斯州成人网站年龄验证法 HB 1181。 该公司是 Verisign，不是该公司的当事方，法官 Maya Guerra Gamble 于 2026 年 6 月 4 日签署了扣押令，四天后在 S​​tate of Texas v Kick Online Entertainment 案中提起诉讼。

该命令指示威瑞信将 motherless.com 置于“注册锁定、保留或类似状态，直至被告回复”，这是运营商缴纳保证金以取回其域名的法律术语。

该域名是被冻结而不是被占用，尽管区别在这里意义不大。 威瑞信实际应用的是serverHold加上服务器级别的删除、转移和更新名称的禁止。 保留会将 motherless.com 从 .com 区域文件中拉出，因此不会对任何人进行解析。

Kick 必须缴纳 9,140,​​000 美元的保证金，该保证金“以被告实施符合德克萨斯州民事实践和补救法典第 129B 章的年龄验证为条件”，并确认它将满足 2024 年 9 月 30 日针对其的民事处罚。 一家在该州管辖范围之外的公司在其财产归还之前必须支付费用并遵守德克萨斯州的法规。 这是州法律的具体表现，是外国运营商通过在登记处扣押资产来拉取的。

法院声称该令状“适当且合理”的理由之一是“被告不是本州居民，而是一家外国公司”，这使得该州无法联系一家公司成为没收其财产的理由。

然后，该命令预先授权了更多相同的内容，最后一行是“应发布国家认为必要的尽可能多的令状”，因此未来扣押的数量由司法部长确定，而不是由法官权衡每一项。 德克萨斯州可以免除这些令状通常要求的担保，因为该命令称“德克萨斯州无需在扣押令状发布之前缴纳保证金”。

获取资产的一方没有发布任何内容。 失败的一方则赔付 914 万美元。

域锁没有边界。 该法律仅适用于德克萨斯州用户，但锁定 .com 会导致地球上每个人都无法使用该网站，包括那些从未通过过此类法律的国家/地区的人们，他们对此没有发言权，也不明白为什么他们必须让德克萨斯州法律影响他们的生活。 国家补救措施之所以具有全球效力，只是因为恰好保存记录的登记处是美国的。

由于更严重的指控，该网站已经离线过一次。 在广播公司 NOS 和 Nieuwsuur 发现该视频托管在荷兰服务器上后，荷兰检察官于 5 月将其撤下，并就涉嫌性虐待视频提起刑事诉讼。 虐待报告局 Offlimits 今年在网站上记录了 142 份报告，其中 25 份涉及儿童。 大约一周后，《Motherless》回归，称其加强了节制。 这次删除是通过其主机到达该网站的，并以刑事案件为依据，德克萨斯州令状通过登记处到达该网站，并以未支付的民事罚款为依据。

这个先例是司法部长想要的，他也是这么说的。 帕克斯顿称该命令是“一个巨大的先例，如果网站无视法律并用色情内容伤害儿童，则可能会被剥夺其域名。”

他的办公室表示，该令状“表明德克萨斯州拥有法律权威和行之有效的工具，可以超越其边界并追究外国运营商的责任”，并且该州将使用“一切可用的法律机制，包括针对域名的扣押令”，针对任何“无论其在何处注册”的公司。 该命令中没有任何内容将该工具限制在色情内容上，因此德克萨斯州针对任何外国网站的民事处罚现在都可以以同样的方式收取。

我们之前曾指出，英国言论监管机构 Ofcom 在针对没有英国业务的美国服务执行《英国在线安全法案》时，存在越界行为，同样的原则也受到威胁。

威瑞信是美国公司，必须服从美国法院，因此法律上的钩子是真实的，而 Ofcom 的钩子则不然。 反对意见并不是说该命令无法无天，而是美国领土上的 .com 注册机构让美国法院获得了整个互联网的开关，而特拉维斯县的一名法官现在已经驳回了该命令。

与英国 Ofcom 案件不同的是，当德克萨斯州法官可以下令关闭一个托管合法内容的网站时，使用美国基础设施及其所谓的第一修正案保护在这里毫无用处，因为它没有引入数字身份功能。

基克从未出庭。 该公司没有对诉讼提出异议，民事处罚已于 2024 年 9 月 30 日默认生效，而且没有法院考虑德克萨斯州针对对方的论点。 保证金条件背后的法规（第 129B 章）是 HB 1181，最高法院去年在言论自由联盟诉 Paxton 案中维持了该法规。 甘布尔的命令是初审法院的一项裁决，对本案之外的任何人都没有约束力。
